prescription.source: R1, R36, R2 (Understanding CrossFit, L1 Guide p. 2; crossfit.com methodology)
prescription.text: CrossFit is a prescription in three parts. Functional movement: the movements you already use daily. High intensity: effort hard enough to make you fitter. Constantly varied: never the same for long. The aim is to prepare you not only for the unknown, but for the unknowable.

functional.source: R15, R8, R9 (Foundations, L1 Guide p. 14; crossfit.com methodology)
functional.text: What makes a movement functional? Life already asks it of you. Squatting is standing from a seated position. Deadlifting is picking any object off the ground. Watch the joints light up: hips, knees and ankles all move together. Natural movement uses many joints at once.

replaced.text: Isolation exercises work one joint at a time, and they have no functional analog in everyday life. So CrossFit swapped them. The lateral raise became the push press. The curl became the pull-up. And the leg extension became the squat. Count the joints.

power.source: R16, R22, R21 (L1 Guide p. 2; Table 1 p. 35; p. 36)
power.text: Intensity is defined exactly as power: work divided by time. Here is Fran, first done in four minutes thirty. The work is constant, so the same work in two minutes forty-five is more power: a 60% increase. Intensity is the variable most tied to adaptation.

varied.text: Now variety. If you only cycle between five and seven miles at each effort, you test weak below five and above seven. Athletes are weakest at the margins of their exposure. Vary the work, and the margins widen: the breadth of adaptation matches the breadth of the stimulus.

pyramid.source: R29, R30 (What Is Fitness? Part 1, L1 Guide p. 29)
pyramid.text: CrossFit builds an athlete in an order: nutrition first, the molecular foundation, then metabolic conditioning for cardiovascular sufficiency, gymnastics for body control, weightlifting and throwing for control of external objects, and finally sport, for mastery and application.

deficiency.text: And here is the rule. We do not deliberately order these components, but nature will. If you have a deficiency at any level of the pyramid, the components above will suffer. Weaken gymnastics, and everything built on it tilts and sinks.

hundred.source: R34 (World-Class Fitness in 100 Words, L1 Guide p. 17)
hundred.text: Fix the weak level, and the pyramid stands again. The whole method fits on it, in a hundred words. Eat meat and vegetables. Bike, run, swim and row, hard and fast. Master the basics of gymnastics. Train the major lifts. And regularly learn and play new sports.
